title: Thrust Lever Assembly Friction Seal and Quadrant Clamp Revision
abstract: Introduces a revised friction seal and quadrant clamp in the thrust lever assembly, correcting a rising breakout force reported by crews on aircraft past three years in service.

sections.reason: Crews on early aircraft reported that the thrust levers had become notchy, needing a deliberate push to start moving and then running free. Measurement on eleven aircraft showed breakout force rising from the delivered value of eighteen newtons to as much as thirty-four, always on aircraft past three years, and always improving briefly after a lubrication. The seal in the quadrant was found to be swelling in contact with the specified lubricant, which is what produces the step in the force.
sections.description: The friction seal in the quadrant is replaced by one in a compound compatible with the specified lubricant, and the quadrant clamp is replaced by a variant with a controlled land that sets the seal compression rather than relying on the clamp torque. The rivets at the clamp interface are changed to the current standard. The lever geometry, the resolver pick-off and the autothrust disconnect switch are all unchanged, so the assembly remains interchangeable and no rerigging is required after embodiment.
sections.effects: Mass change is negligible. No electrical load change. Interchangeable at assembly level. Breakout force returns to the delivered range and the lubrication interval is extended from twelve to twenty-four months, which is a maintenance planning change for operators. The inspection task is reissued with the revised force check, and the autothrust description entry is reviewed but not changed.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in at MSN M00456. Retrofit is by bulletin at any base visit, about eight hours with the pedestal open, and is normally combined with the scheduled lubrication.

type_data.production_impact: Cut in at MSN M00456, pedestal build unchanged
